budgets.title: Budgets
budgets.subtitle: Budget management and financial risk analysis
budgets.introPara: The Budgets panel is an essential tool for financial planning and control, allowing you to set spending goals and track consumption against the established budget.
budgets.introAlert: Important: Budgets enable proactive cost control, with automatic alerts when consumption approaches or exceeds defined limits.
budgets.budgetsDesc: Creation and management of main budgets
budgets.subBudgetsDesc: Division of budgets into smaller categories
budgets.riskAnalysisDesc: Forecasting and identification of financial risks
budgets.creatingManagingPara: Budgets allow setting spending limits for different periods, VDCs, services or projects, providing granular financial control.
budgets.creatingBudgetStep3: Fill in budget name and description
budgets.creatingBudgetStep6: Choose scope (Entire Contract, Specific VDC, Tags, etc.)
budgets.budgetFixoDesc: Fixed value that remains constant throughout the period (e.g., R$ 10,000/month).
budgets.budgetVariavelDesc: Value that varies according to historical average or planned growth.
budgets.budgetProjetoDesc: Specific budget for a project with defined start and end dates.
budgets.budgetRecorrenteDesc: Budget that automatically renews each period (monthly, quarterly).
budgets.alertConfigPara: Configure notifications for different consumption levels:
budgets.alert50Desc: Preventive alert - spending reached half of the budget
budgets.alertForecastDesc: Alert when projection indicates future overshoot
budgets.budgetViewProjection: Consumption projection until end of period
budgets.subBudgetPara: Sub-Budgets allow dividing a main budget into smaller categories, facilitating granular control and resource allocation by department, project or service type.
budgets.subBudgetHierarchyPara: Example of budget division of R$ 100,000/month:
budgets.subBudgetCreatingStep3: Set name and value (cannot exceed parent budget)
budgets.subBudgetSumRulesAlert: Important: The sum of sub-budgets cannot exceed the main budget. If adjustment is needed, first increase the parent budget or reduce other sub-budgets.

budgets.riskMediumDesc: Accelerated consumption. Projection indicates 85-100% budget utilization. Attention recommended.
budgets.riskHighDesc: Critical consumption. Projection indicates budget overshoot (>100%). Immediate action required.

budgets.riskFactorSeasonality: Seasonality: Historical patterns from the same period in previous years

budgets.riskProjectionAggressiveDesc: Considers worst-case scenario with consumption acceleration
budgets.riskRecommendationsPara: When risk is detected, the platform suggests actions:

budgets.riskRecommendation5: Increase budget or reallocate from other areas

franquia.relatorioRecursoDesc: Breaks down USN consumption by category (Compute, Storage, Network), identifying where the largest franchise consumption occurs.

regrasFinanceiro.title: Finance Rules
regrasFinanceiro.subtitle: Financial rules configuration and management for cloud contracts
regrasFinanceiro.accessText: To access the Finance Rules card, click on the Administration menu on the left side of the screen. The Contracts option must be selected.
regrasFinanceiro.accessText2: The listing shows contract names, administrators, CPF/CNPJ number, contract status (active or inactive), and an actions column that allows cloning the selected contract information.
regrasFinanceiro.cardRegrasDesc: The card contains the following items:
regrasFinanceiro.cardItem1: Billing Rule — defines how costs are calculated and billed
regrasFinanceiro.cardItem2: Rate and Quotation — exchange conversion parameters and applied rates
regrasFinanceiro.cardItem3: Billing History — chronological record of billings performed
regrasFinanceiro.cardItem4: Tags — association of tags to billing rules
regrasFinanceiro.billingRuleDesc: This feature is related to the information present in Billing reports, highlighting the usage value generated by clouds and the billing rule(s) created in the uCloud portal.
regrasFinanceiro.billingRuleNote: In this billing process, the platform uses the value consumed by the user in the cloud and the defined billing rule as reference. There is no maximum limit for the number of billing rules that can be created in a contract.
regrasFinanceiro.creatingBillingRuleDesc: Fill in the fields: Rule Name, Type (Markup, Discount, Fixed Rate), Value/Percentage, Associated Contracts, and Validity Period.
regrasFinanceiro.billingRuleByTagDesc: In the "Billing rules by tag" field, the platform displays a modal that allows the user to include TAGS in the created billing rules, registering fixed financial rates per Tag.
regrasFinanceiro.billingRuleByTagNote: If no Tag is registered with a specific value, the platform uses the normal billing history value linked to the contract.
regrasFinanceiro.updateListingDesc: The listing updates automatically after creating, editing, or deleting a rule. Use the update button if needed.

visaoGeral.title: Overview
visaoGeral.financeDesc: Introduction to Financial Governance on the uCloud platform
visaoGeral.financeIntroPara1: This manual begins by describing the five areas of action of the uCloud platform: financial governance, service billing, infrastructure monitoring, inventory, and infrastructure operation.
visaoGeral.financeIntroPara2: This section is dedicated to the "Finance" topic. It is important to note that the platform does not create or generate computational resource values - these values are generated by public cloud providers.
visaoGeral.financeHowToUse: The uCloud platform extracts billing data from public cloud providers' billing files, downloading the values generated by the use of computational resources. It then adds this information to its internal databases and subsequently applies calculated costs converted to local currency in Brazil.
visaoGeral.financeNoCustomization: The uCloud platform provides a ready-to-use cost visualization interface. Users do not need to create or customize any existing views, with some exceptions where the report allows customizing the period and detailed information about tagged resources.
visaoGeral.userProfilesDesc: The Finance menu is visible to any user profile. Below are the profile types:
visaoGeral.normalUserDesc: This profile views their own consumption and that of their contract.
visaoGeral.contractAdminDesc: Views information for all groups and users linked to the contract.
visaoGeral.groupAdminDesc: Views information for the group(s) they are linked to and all users linked to the group.
visaoGeral.privateCompaniesPara1: For the corporate environment, the uCloud platform downloads lines from the billing file (also known as the bucket) from the cloud service provider. This file is an ASCII text file with comma-separated data (.csv format).
visaoGeral.privateCompaniesPara2: The uCloud platform syncs the content of this file into its internal databases and calculates the conversion of values for the period, using them according to the information entered in the following Contract fields:
visaoGeral.privateCompaniesItem4: Currency quotation day (valid for variable quotation - uses the PTAX rate from the Brazilian Central Bank)
visaoGeral.conversionFormulaFixedValue: BRL Value = Total USD Value × [Fixed] Dollar Rate × Billing Rate
visaoGeral.conversionFormulaVariableValue: BRL Value = Total USD Value × [Day] PTAX Rate × Billing Rate
visaoGeral.importantDesc: For providers that store values in Brazilian Reais, the Contract Administrator user must change the Currency field to 1.00 and Quotation Type to FIXED.
visaoGeral.warningDesc: Tax amounts for invoice issuance in Brazilian territory are not presented by any provider and are also not calculated by the uCloud platform. Tax amounts are calculated by the issuer of the final Invoice document.
visaoGeral.publicCompaniesPara1: Due to the constant variation of the exchange rate (Dollar ↔ Real), the Brazilian Federal Government created an intelligent and simplified format to control its budget limits for public cloud computing, ensuring it never breaches the limits of the Budgetary Guidelines Law (LDO).
visaoGeral.usnUnitDesc: It is a cloud service pricing model designed for entities and bodies within the Brazilian government sphere. It aims to establish itself as a predictable, linear, and flexible method for obtaining a specific amount charged for cloud computing services.
visaoGeral.usnUnitPara2: This unique approach allows any Brazilian Government entity (Federal, State, or Municipal) to consume public cloud computing resources, allowing the value of USN services to be calculated using the commercial dollar price on the trading day, fixed throughout the contract.
visaoGeral.usnCalculationItem1: The sum of the used quantity of the resource is multiplied by the defined price
visaoGeral.usnCalculationItem2: For virtual machines, the price is multiplied by the CPU quantity or memory amount in GB
visaoGeral.usnCalculationItem3: What defines whether this calculation will be by CPU or memory is the tag applied to the resources
visaoGeral.usnCalculationItem4: If the USN tag type does not exist on the resource, the calculation is not performed
visaoGeral.usnConversionFormulaFixedValue: BRL Value = USN Resource Value/h × Monthly USN Total × [Fixed] USD Value × Billing Rate
visaoGeral.usnConversionFormulaVariableValue: BRL Value = USN Resource Value/h × Monthly USN Total × [Day] USD PTAX × Billing Rate
visaoGeral.corporateEnvironmentPara1: The Contract is the main point where the uCloud platform user organization establishes how it manages commercial aspects, financial limits (or computational resource limits), defines values for computational resources individually, and links groups and users.
visaoGeral.corporateEnvironmentItem1: Conversion method from foreign currency to local currency
visaoGeral.corporateEnvironmentItem2: Whether the conversion value is fixed or variable
visaoGeral.corporateEnvironmentItem3: Tax rates applied to contract costs
visaoGeral.importantNoteDesc: All report screens presented in this document show values being converted to Brazilian Real (BRL), as configured in the Contract.
visaoGeral.financialPanelsDesc: The uCloud platform presents reports based on two different financial concepts:
visaoGeral.consumptionPanelsDesc: Refers to accumulated values of computational resources consumed/used in the current month up to the current day or until the last processing period of values by the provider.
visaoGeral.processingWindowDesc: The term "window" refers to the period in which the provider records computational resource values in the Bucket file. The average time of this window is around twelve (12) hours.
visaoGeral.invoicePanelsDesc: Shows the total consumption value of computational resources from the cloud service provider (public/private) only from the period up to the previous month of the current month.
visaoGeral.exampleDesc: A contract with billing date on the 8th. The August invoice is on the 8th and refers to values consumed throughout the previous month (July 8th to August 7th).
visaoGeral.invoiceMonth: The uCloud platform establishes the billing month period using the "Invoice Day" field in the Billing Rules section of the Contract.

financeiro.title: Finance
financeiro.subtitle: Consolidated and detailed billing view by contract, group, and user
financeiro.overview: The Finance module is located in the left sidebar, within the Cost Management section. It centralizes all billing information for the selected contract, allowing the user to view total consumption, associated groups, responsible users, and details of each billed item — including credits, taxes, and tags.
financeiro.howToAccessDesc: In the left sidebar, click on Finance (identified by the dollar sign icon). The main page will load with the title "Finance – Here you will see billing information for the selected contract".
financeiro.step1Title: Step 1 — Selecting the contract and period
financeiro.step1Desc: When entering the module, you will see the "Select a contract to start" panel. It has two required fields:
financeiro.step1Field1Desc: Use the dropdown menu to choose the desired contract. Available contracts are listed by identifier.
financeiro.step1Field2Desc: Select the reference month/year in MM/YYYY format (e.g., 05/2026). You can type or use the calendar icon.
financeiro.step1Action: After filling in both fields, click the Search button (red). The system will load billing information for the contract and period entered.
financeiro.step1ImageAlt: Finance module initial screen with contract and period selection
financeiro.step2Desc: After searching, the module displays a panel divided into three main blocks:
financeiro.step2InvoiceIntro: Consolidated financial summary of the contract, with the following values:
financeiro.step2GroupsDesc: Lists the groups linked to the contract with each group's consumption value. Each group is a clickable link to access detail level. Use the Previous and Next buttons to navigate between groups when there is more than one.
financeiro.step2ChartDesc: Donut chart that visually represents the percentage distribution of consumption among contract groups. The legend identifies each group by its corresponding color.
financeiro.step2ImageAlt: Contract Invoice panel with Groups and Consumption by group chart
financeiro.step3Title: Step 3 — Resource Consumption during the Month
financeiro.step3Desc: Below the invoice panel, the module displays a bar chart titled "Resource consumption during the month". This chart shows the monthly consumption evolution in the contract currency over recent months, with each bar representing a period and each color representing a different group. It helps identify growth or reduction trends over time.
financeiro.step4Desc: When clicking a group name (underlined link in the "Groups" section), the system navigates to that group's detail page. This page shows:
financeiro.step4ImageAlt: Monthly consumption and distribution charts and group login/user table
financeiro.step5Desc: When clicking a login in the table, the system navigates to the user's invoice page. This page shows:
financeiro.step5UserInvoiceIntro: Financial summary of the user/account in the period:
financeiro.step5ResourcesDesc: Bar chart showing the historical consumption evolution of that user over recent months.
financeiro.step5Tip: Tip: The filter icon in the upper right corner of the page loads/updates the financial data of the selected user. Click it if values appear as "Not available".
financeiro.step5CardsDesc: Below the main panel, there are four detail cards:
financeiro.hierarchyDesc: The Finance module follows this hierarchy:
financeiro.step2InvoiceItem1Desc: total amount billed in the period
financeiro.step2InvoiceItem4Desc: cost of services acquired via marketplace
financeiro.step2InvoiceItem6Desc: exchange rate used for BRL conversion
financeiro.step2InvoiceItem7Desc: exchange rate applied to marketplace items
financeiro.step2InvoiceItem8Desc: date range (start to end of month) covered by the invoice
financeiro.step4Detail1: Contract Invoice (group level): total consumption, rates, and period for that group only.
financeiro.step4Detail2: Groups (sub-groups): lists linked groups or sub-accounts with pagination navigation.
financeiro.step4Detail3: Consumption by group: donut chart with visual distribution by sub-group.
financeiro.step4Detail4: Resource consumption during the month: bar chart with historical consumption evolution of that group.
financeiro.step4Detail5: Resource distribution during the month: segmented bar chart with three columns — Consumption, Tax, and Credit — showing cost composition.
financeiro.step4Detail6: Login/User Table: displayed at the bottom, with Login (user identifier or connector account) and Value (associated cost in the period) columns. Each login is clickable with pagination.
financeiro.step5ImageAlt: User Invoice screen with Consumed Resources chart and Billed Items, Credits, Taxes, and Tags cards
financeiro.step5Card1Desc: Total value of charged items. The + Details button opens listing with: Product Name, Detail, Quantity, Start/End Date, and Cost.
financeiro.step5Card2Desc: Total value of applied credits. The + Details button opens listing with: Product Name, Start/End Date, and Cost.
financeiro.step5Card3Desc: Total tax amount. The + Details button opens listing with: Product Name, Start/End Date, and Cost.
financeiro.step5Card4Desc: Views cost distributed by tags assigned to resources. The + Details button opens 'Items by Tag' page with: Tag, Cost, and Actions.
financeiro.navItem1: Back: at any level, the arrow icon (←) at the top returns to the previous hierarchy level (contract → group → user → detail).
financeiro.navItem2: Table sorting: columns can be sorted by clicking the header. The ⬆⬇ icon indicates a sortable column; ⬇ indicates active sorting.
financeiro.navItem3: Pagination: all tables have first page («), previous page (‹), next page (›), and last page (») controls.
financeiro.navItem4: Products section: on the main contract screen, there is an expandable Products section. The + icon next to the title expands the section to view associated contract products.
financeiro.hierarchyItem1: Finance (contract) → select contract + period → view consolidated invoice, groups, and charts.
financeiro.hierarchyItem2: Group → click the group → view consumption, distribution by categories, and login list.
financeiro.hierarchyItem3: User/Login → click login → view user invoice and the four detail cards.
financeiro.hierarchyItem4: Detailed items → click "+ Details" on any card → opens specific listing of billed items, credits, taxes, or tags.

consolidadoFaturamento.title: Consolidated Billing
consolidadoFaturamento.subtitle: Centralized invoice history with lifecycle control, inline details, and navigation to the Finance module
consolidadoFaturamento.overview: Consolidated Billing centralizes the invoice history of all user contracts, allowing consultation, detailed visualization, lifecycle control (opening and closing), and quick access to financial details per invoice.
consolidadoFaturamento.overviewNote: Clients with multiple contracts and providers can, from a single point, consult and monitor all consolidated invoices by period.
consolidadoFaturamento.contractListDesc: Multiselect dropdown with checkbox and search field. Includes "Select all" option as the first item for scenarios with more than one available. The session's global contract is pre-selected by default.
consolidadoFaturamento.periodDesc: Month range selector. Display format: MM/YYYY to MM/YYYY. The "Search" button is disabled while the period is not selected.
consolidadoFaturamento.tableCompetenciaPeriodo: Competence vs. Period: The 01/2026 competence invoice covers the period 01/12/2025 - 31/12/2025 — the competence is shifted 1 month relative to the consumption period.
consolidadoFaturamento.actionReopenDesc: Available for Closed invoices. Reopens the invoice and changes status to Open.
consolidadoFaturamento.actionCloseDesc: Available for Open invoices. Closes the invoice and records the closing date/time.
consolidadoFaturamento.actionDetailsDesc: Opens the 'Finance' module with pre-loaded invoice parameters (month, year). Available for all invoices.
consolidadoFaturamento.actionOnScreenDesc: Opens "Financial Details" modal inline without leaving the current screen. Available for all invoices.
consolidadoFaturamento.modalDesc: Displayed when clicking "On Screen". Supports minimization and closing via × button.
consolidadoFaturamento.modalViewResource: Resource: groups by service/product (e.g., Amazon EC2, AWS Lambda)
consolidadoFaturamento.modalTableDesc: Columns: Resource | Total (USD) | Total (BRL). Expandable hierarchy by account with ▼/▶ button.
consolidadoFaturamento.paginationItemsDesc: Options: 5, 10 (default), 20, 50, 100. Counter: Showing X - Y of Z results
consolidadoFaturamento.mainImageAlt: Consolidated Billing screen showing contract selection, period, and invoice table
consolidadoFaturamento.tableRowContractDesc: Total value in R$ (Provider Currency) with 2 decimal places
consolidadoFaturamento.tableRowPeriodDesc: Consumption date range — DD/MM/YYYY HH:MM:SS - DD/MM/YYYY HH:MM:SS
consolidadoFaturamento.tableRowClosingDesc: Closing date and time. Empty + tooltip if invoice is open
consolidadoFaturamento.tableRowPriceDesc: Total value in R$ with 2 decimal places
consolidadoFaturamento.tableRowActionsDesc: 2 or 3 icons according to invoice status

contaMaster.title: Master Account
contaMaster.subtitle: View Master Account spending and associated Linked Accounts
contaMaster.overviewText: Master Account is a financial visibility module within the Cost Management product. It consolidates and presents the spending of a main cloud provider account together with all associated sub-accounts, allowing navigation through the cost hierarchy from the most aggregated to the most granular level.
contaMaster.goalBoxText: Perform complete financial drill-down analysis of the account, examining costs in greater detail.
contaMaster.contractSelectorDesc: Dropdown with text search field. Lists available contracts for the authenticated user. The selected contract here defines which Master Account will be displayed, regardless of global context.
contaMaster.periodDesc: Monthly granularity (MM/YYYY). Default: current month. The query is not automatic, meaning the user must click "Filter" after selecting contract and period.
contaMaster.resumoCardDesc: After applying the filter, the card displays:
contaMaster.tableHierarchicDesc: The table is organized in an expandable hierarchy with 5 levels:
contaMaster.tableColumnsDesc: SUB-ACCOUNTS (with visual indentation per level) · TOTAL (CONTRACT CURRENCY) with 4 decimal places · PROVIDER CURRENCY (USD) with 4 decimal places
contaMaster.decimalNote: All values are displayed with 4 decimal places (e.g., R$ 2,835.7941 / $521.5183), ensuring fractional cost precision. This requires configuration via the Finance Rules card in the Administration > Contracts > Choose contract menu.
contaMaster.awsServicesZeroCost: Zero-cost services are displayed normally, confirming the service exists but generated no cost in the period.
contaMaster.tableAlt: Example of the hierarchical Cost Information table
contaMaster.resumoCardTotalDesc: Original value in provider currency (usually USD for AWS, EUR for Azure, depends on client)
contaMaster.resumoCardCurrencyDesc: Original value in provider currency (USD for AWS, EUR for Azure)
contaMaster.resumoCardRateDesc: Exchange rate used for conversion, in red (e.g., $4.99). Obtained via API for the effective period date.
contaMaster.hierarchicLevel3Desc: Region name or 'No Region' for global services
contaMaster.mainFlowStep2: System checks JWT token and loads user's contract list
contaMaster.mainFlowStep3: Pre-selects active contract from global context and current month
contaMaster.mainFlowStep4: Fetches dollar rate for current month via dedicated API
contaMaster.mainFlowStep5: Renders summary card and table with collapsed sub-accounts
contaMaster.mainFlowStep6: User clicks arrow on a sub-account → expands to see services
contaMaster.mainFlowStep7: Continues expanding to individual SKU levels (level 5)
contaMaster.switchContractStep2: Select new contract in dropdown with text search

custoBudget.title: Budget Cost
custoBudget.subtitle: Define and track budgets in real-time, comparing with consumption
custoBudget.overviewText: Budget Cost allows financial and technology managers to define budgets for cloud contracts and track real-time consumption against the planned value. The system emits visual warning signals when consumption approaches or exceeds established limits.
custoBudget.semaforoNote: The system does not prevent consumption from exceeding the total value — it only signals visually. The % can exceed 100% (e.g., 3,843,887.22% observed in production).
custoBudget.formulaText: Formula: % Consumed = (Consumed Value / Total Value) × 100. Pagination: 5, 10 (default), 20, 50, 100 items.
custoBudget.formSections: Form divided into 3 sections + Summary side panel.
custoBudget.editingBudgetDesc: Same creation form with pre-loaded data. "Edit Budget" button instead of "Save Budget". The same Balance = R$ 0.00 rule applies. Success toast: "Budget edited successfully!"
custoBudget.deletingBudgetDesc: Confirmation modal with message: "This action cannot be undone. Are you sure you want to delete this budget?" Deletion is permanent and immediate — no archiving.
custoBudget.custoBudgetTelaAlt: Budget Cost screen — contract selection and budget listing
custoBudget.criarNovoAlt: "Create new Budget" screen — general information, allocation, and summary panel
custoBudget.editarAlt: "Edit Budget" screen — pre-loaded data with existing allocations
custoBudget.excluirAlt: Confirmation modal when deleting a Budget
custoBudget.painelResumoAlt: Summary Panel displayed during budget creation/editing
custoBudget.recorrenciaAlt: Email alert configuration and Budget recurrence
custoBudget.role1Desc: Sets monthly/quarterly budgets and monitors adherence.
custoBudget.role2Desc: Tracks consumption by Account Provider and approved budget.
custoBudget.role3Desc: Configures budgets and receives email alerts.
custoBudget.budgetTableFavDesc: Star icon — empty = not favorited; golden filled = favorited
custoBudget.budgetTableIntervalDesc: Monthly, Quarterly, Semi-annual, Annual or --- (no recurrence)
custoBudget.budgetTablePctDesc: Percentage of total value consumed (with traffic light color)
custoBudget.formAllocation1: Specification: Account Provider, Master Account, Cloud, Dimension, Tag
custoBudget.formAllocation3: "Allocate Budget" button — enables when value > R$ 0
custoBudget.formRecurrence2: Recurring budget (automatic creation at the end of each period)
custoBudget.createRule: Mandatory Rule: The "Save Budget" button is only enabled when Balance = R$ 0.00 (Total Value = Allocated Value). The user must distribute the entire value before saving. The Billing method is locked after the first allocation.
custoBudget.resumoBalanceDesc: Green when positive. Must be R$ 0.00 to save.
custoBudget.alertSystemDesc: When enabling "Routine Alert", an automatic routine monitors the budget and sends email alerts.
custoBudget.favoritesDesc: Each budget has a clickable star: empty = not favorited; golden filled = favorited. The action is instant, no confirmation.
custoBudget.flowStep2: Click "New Budget" → navigate to creation form
custoBudget.flowStep3: Fill in Budget Name → Summary updates in real time
custoBudget.flowStep5: Select Billing method and fill in Total Value
custoBudget.flowStep6: In Allocation section: select Specification → select provider → fill value → click "Allocate Budget"
custoBudget.flowStep8: Configure Recurrence and Alerts if desired
custoBudget.flowStep9: "Save Budget" button activates when Balance = R$ 0.00 → success toast

custoRelacionalProduto.title: Product Relational Cost
custoRelacionalProduto.subtitle: Module: Cost Management · Side menu > Product Relational Cost
custoRelacionalProduto.overviewText: Product Relational Cost is a reporting feature that allows viewing and detailing cloud resource and sub-resource spending, organized by product and product family. It enables understanding exactly where money is being spent within a contract, cross-referencing contract, cloud provider, product, and linked accounts.
custoRelacionalProduto.overviewText2: The feature is especially useful for FinOps teams, contract managers, and those responsible for cost allocation, as it provides granularity in spending analysis, facilitating identification of consumption by service, sub-service, and period.
custoRelacionalProduto.howItWorksDesc: Using the feature is divided into two sequential steps, visually represented by numbered stages in the interface.
custoRelacionalProduto.step1: Select contract parameters and desired period
custoRelacionalProduto.step1Desc: In this first step, you define the general scope of the query. All fields must be filled before proceeding.
custoRelacionalProduto.step1Interval: Interval — Defines the temporal granularity of the report.
custoRelacionalProduto.step1IntervalMensal: Monthly: groups data month by month. Ideal for trend analysis.
custoRelacionalProduto.step1IntervalSemanal: Weekly: groups data by week. Useful for short-term variations.
custoRelacionalProduto.step1IntervalDiario: Daily: displays data day by day, with greater operational level.
custoRelacionalProduto.step1Periodo: Period — Defines the date range to be queried. Clicking the field displays a month selector to choose the desired month and year.
custoRelacionalProduto.step1Contratos: Contract list — Select the contract to analyze. The system automatically loads the contract associated with the logged-in profile, but it can be changed via dropdown if the user has access to multiple contracts.
custoRelacionalProduto.step1Provider: Account Provider — Select the cloud provider linked to the contract (e.g., AWS, Azure, GCP).
custoRelacionalProduto.step1Action: After filling all fields, click Proceed to unlock Step 2. The Clear button resets all fields in this step.
custoRelacionalProduto.step2Desc: With the contract context defined, this step allows refining the query by applying specific product and account filters.
custoRelacionalProduto.step2Linkeds: Linkeds — Filters data by linked accounts (sub-accounts associated with the contract). Allows segmenting cost by business unit, project, or environment (e.g., production, staging).
custoRelacionalProduto.step2Produto: Product — Select the cloud service you want to analyze (e.g., EC2, S3, RDS on AWS).
custoRelacionalProduto.step2Familia: Product family — Groups products by category, allowing a consolidated view of a set of related services.
custoRelacionalProduto.step2Action: After defining the filters, click Search to generate the report. The Clear button resets the filters in this step without changing Step 1 parameters.
custoRelacionalProduto.flowStep1: Access Cost Management > Product Relational Cost in the side menu.
custoRelacionalProduto.flowStep4: In Step 2, apply filters for Linkeds, Product and/or Product family.
custoRelacionalProduto.flowStep5: Click Search to generate the detailed cost report.
custoRelacionalProduto.useCase1Desc: Use the Linkeds filter to identify each account/project consumption and distribute costs internally.
custoRelacionalProduto.useCase2Desc: Filter by Product to understand how much is being spent on a specific cloud resource.
custoRelacionalProduto.useCase3Desc: Use Product family to group related services and have a macro view of spending.
custoRelacionalProduto.useCase4Desc: Change the Interval to Monthly or Weekly and compare distinct periods to identify consumption variations.
custoRelacionalProduto.tip: Tip: If the "Proceed" button in Step 1 is disabled, check that all required fields are filled: Interval, Period, Contract list, and Account Provider.
custoRelacionalProduto.mainAlt: Product Relational Cost screen with steps 1 and 2
custoRelacionalProduto.resultAlt: Report result with cost by linked graph and product table

exportarRelatorios.title: Export Reports
exportarRelatorios.subtitle: Asynchronous generation of financial files with export history and email notification
exportarRelatorios.overviewText: The 'Export Reports' module allows users to asynchronously generate financial data and cloud consumption files in different formats, based on configurable parameters by report type. After generation, files become available for download and an export history is maintained for reuse.
exportarRelatorios.commonFieldsDesc: All reports share the base fields: Contract (dropdown with search), Period (month/year), and Report Type (defines file structure).
exportarRelatorios.reportTypesList: Available types: Consumption Report (active resource details), Invoice Report (billed values), Cost by Tag Report (distribution by tags), and Budget Report (budget tracking).
exportarRelatorios.validationsDesc: Required fields: Contract, Period, and Report Type. Default output format is CSV; XLSX and PDF available depending on type.
exportarRelatorios.asyncProcessingDesc: The report is generated in the background. The user receives an email notification when the file is ready for download. Large reports may take a few minutes.
exportarRelatorios.exportHistoryDesc: The History section displays all requested exports with: Date/Time, Report Type, Period, Status (Processing, Completed, Error) and download link. History is kept for 30 days.
exportarRelatorios.mainFlowSteps: 1. Access Export Reports in Cost Management menu · 2. Fill in the form fields · 3. Click "Generate Report" · 4. Track status in History · 5. Download when completed

historicoServico.title: Service History
historicoServico.subtitle: Detailed tracking of services consumed in the period
historicoServico.overviewText: Service History allows detailed viewing of all services consumed within a contract in a given period, presenting information such as resource identifier, provider, family, product, VDC (Virtual Data Center), region, and associated values.
historicoServico.overviewText2: The main Service History screen is divided into two main areas: a complete data table and a financial summary panel at the top.
historicoServico.tableColumnsDesc: The table displays the following information for each consumption line:
historicoServico.colRecurso: Resource — Name or identifier of the consumed resource
historicoServico.colProvider: Provider — Cloud provider (AWS, Azure, GCP, etc.)
historicoServico.colFamilia: Family — Service category (e.g., Compute, Storage, Network)
historicoServico.colProduto: Product — Specific service (e.g., EC2, S3, RDS)
historicoServico.colVDC: VDC — Virtual Data Center where the resource is allocated
historicoServico.colRegiao: Region — Geographic region of the resource
historicoServico.colCusto: Cost — Resource cost value in the period
historicoServico.colValor: Final Value — Total value after applying financial rules
historicoServico.summaryTotalCost: Total Cost — Sum of costs of all listed resources
historicoServico.summaryTotalCredits: Total Credits — Sum of applied credits
historicoServico.summaryFinalValue: Final Value — Total cost minus credits
historicoServico.actionFilter: Filter — Refine data by provider, family, product, etc.
historicoServico.actionExport: Export — Download data in CSV or XLSX
historicoServico.actionDetails: Details — Expand row to view sub-resources

tendenciaFaturamento.title: Billing Trend
tendenciaFaturamento.subtitle: Predictive billing analysis based on historical consumption data
tendenciaFaturamento.overviewText: Billing Trend is an analytical tool that uses historical consumption data to project future billing values, enabling financial planning and early identification of significant variations.
tendenciaFaturamento.overviewText2: The analysis considers multiple variables such as seasonal patterns, organic growth, price changes, and consumption behavior from recent periods to generate accurate projections.
tendenciaFaturamento.projectionShortDesc: Projection based on consumption from the last 30 days with adjustments for immediate trend. Ideal for operational planning and quick budget adjustments.
tendenciaFaturamento.projectionMediumDesc: Uses weighted average of the last 3 months, considering growth or reduction trends. Recommended for tactical planning.
tendenciaFaturamento.projectionLongDesc: Annual projection considering seasonalities and historical patterns. Suitable for strategic planning and annual budget definition.
tendenciaFaturamento.factorHistorical: Consumption History — Last 12 months of billing data
tendenciaFaturamento.factorSeasonality: Seasonality — Consumption patterns that repeat at certain times
tendenciaFaturamento.factorGrowth: Growth Rate — Average percentage variation between periods
tendenciaFaturamento.factorResources: New Resources — Impact of recently added or removed resources
tendenciaFaturamento.factorPricing: Price Changes — Changes in provider pricing tables
tendenciaFaturamento.factorContracts: Contract Changes — Contract changes affecting billing

gpon360.title: Incognito - GPON 360
gpon360.subtitle: Product Documentation
gpon360.clientsDescription: Query and management of the client base connected to the GPON network.
gpon360.dashboardsDescription: Consolidated panels with key network indicators.
gpon360.signalMonitoringDescription: Tracking of optical signal levels (RX/TX) of terminals.
gpon360.massiveTrapDescription: Detection and handling of massive events received via SNMP trap.
gpon360.fallMonitoringDescription: Identification of drops, instabilities, and recurrences in the network.
gpon360.performanceDescription: Performance metrics such as latency, jitter, loss, and throughput.
gpon360.reportsDescription: Generation and export of operational and managerial reports.
gpon360.parameterManagementDescription: Configuration of parameters and thresholds used in analyses.
gpon360.auditDescription: Record and traceability of actions performed on the platform.
gpon360.step1Desc: The user filters and locates the desired client on the Clients screen using any combination of available criteria.
gpon360.step2Desc: Click Connect to open the complete diagnostics for that equipment.
gpon360.step3Desc: From there, investigate signal, quality of service, Wi-Fi configuration, and network topology, all in a single centralized panel.
gpon360.searchRules: Usage rule: it is not necessary to fill in all fields, but at least one criterion must be provided for the search to be executed.
gpon360.filterImageAlt: Fall Monitoring filter interface showing State, City, Drop Type, OLT, and period
gpon360.resultsImageAlt: Results table on the Clients screen
gpon360.overviewDesc: Documentation for this module will be published soon.
gpon360.clientsIntro: The Clients screen is the starting point of the GPON module to locate and inspect any equipment (ONT/ONU) installed in the client base. It brings together a very robust base, with more than 3.1 million records distributed in a paginated table, allowing the operator to quickly find a specific client and, from there, open the complete diagnostics panel for that modem.
gpon360.clientsFilterDesc: At the top of the page is the Filters block, where the user can search by operator code, MAC address, contract number, city, terminal model, or Node/OLT identification. There are also two complementary selectors: one filters by the Brazilian state (UF) where the client is located, and the other filters by connection status, showing only Active or Inactive equipment.
gpon360.clientsSearchRule: Usage rule: it is not necessary to fill in all fields, but at least one criterion must be provided for the search to be executed.
gpon360.clientsSearchButtonsDesc: The Search and Clear buttons complete this block, allowing you to apply the filter or reset all fields at once.
gpon360.clientsTableDesc: Below the filters, the client list is displayed in table format, bringing for each row information such as contract, operator code, MAC address, status, terminal model, contracted download and upload speeds, Node/OLT, as well as location data such as ZIP code, city, state, and full address.
gpon360.clientsTablePaginationDesc: Since the database is very extensive, navigation is done through pagination, with control over how many items to display per page and a clear indication of "current page of total pages", which helps users not get lost when browsing large volumes of data.
gpon360.modemInfoDesc: Panel with essential client equipment data: status, TX/RX signal levels, GPON technology, last recorded event and its cause. Also displays identification such as Node/OLT, MAC address, contract, Up Time, city, model, serial, CPU, memory, and software version.
gpon360.qosGeneralDesc: Consolidated score of the client experience.
gpon360.qosAvailabilityDesc: Percentage of time with service available.
gpon360.qosHistoryNote: Just like the signal indicators, each card has its own History button, which opens a window showing the evolution of these scores over the chosen period — very useful to identify if the client's connection quality is getting worse or better over time.
gpon360.speedTestIntro: In this same area you will find two highlighted cards: Run speed test, which allows you to trigger a new test directly on the client's equipment, and Test history, which opens a window with a summary of measurements already taken, including download and upload graphs compared to the contracted value.
gpon360.speedTestSpeeds: Right below these cards, the Contractual and measured speeds section shows two visual speedometers, one for download and one for upload, comparing the measured speed with the speed contracted by the client.
gpon360.speedTestWarning: Warning: if any of these values appear as zero, it's a sign that it's worth running a new speed test to update the information.
gpon360.wifiNetworksDesc: The dashboard also displays two side-by-side cards with the client's wireless network settings, one for 2.4 GHz and another for 5.0 GHz. In each card you can see whether the network is active, the network name (SSID), the channel in use, the configured security type (such as WPA2-Personal), the channel width, and the supported protocols.
gpon360.wifiEditDesc: If you need to change the network name or password, there is an Edit link in each card, which opens a small window to set a new name and password for that specific network.
gpon360.connectedDevicesIntro: Finally, at the bottom of the screen, there is the Equipment section, which brings together three very useful features for diagnosis.
gpon360.connectedDevices1Desc: Shows the number of devices found on the network and, when clicking Access, opens a table with name, type (router, cell phone, unknown, etc.), MAC, IP, connection type (2.4 GHz, 5.0 GHz, or Ethernet), and signal strength indicated by colors.
gpon360.connectedDevices2Desc: Displays a visual diagram with the router in the center and the connected devices around it, with a color legend indicating whether the connection is good, fair, or poor, in addition to the type of connection used.
gpon360.connectedDevices3Desc: Focuses on devices with weak or distant signal from the router, helping to quickly identify possible improvement points in the client's Wi-Fi coverage.
gpon360.searchDashboardDesc1: It all starts in the sidebar menu, in the Dashboard option. When accessing, the system asks you to choose a search type: by MAC Address or by Contract Number. After selecting the desired option, you type the operator code (the "city code" of the client's city) and the corresponding search data, and click Search.
gpon360.searchDashboardDesc2: The system then returns the found result, and you just click Select to open the complete view of that client. If you need to search for another client later, there is always a New search button at the top of the screen to restart the search without leaving the page.
gpon360.searchDashboardImageAlt: Client search screen by MAC Address or Contract Number
gpon360.searchDashboardImageCaption: Client search screen by MAC Address or Contract Number
gpon360.qosImageAlt: Quality indicator (QoS) cards for the client
gpon360.qosImageCaption: Quality indicator (QoS) cards for the client
gpon360.speedTestImageAlt: Speed test screen with action cards, speedometers, and measurement history
gpon360.speedTestImageCaption: Speed test screen with speedometers and measurement history
gpon360.wifiImageAlt: Wi-Fi network configuration cards for 2.4 GHz and 5.0 GHz
gpon360.wifiImageCaption: Wi-Fi network configuration cards for 2.4 GHz and 5.0 GHz
gpon360.equipamentosImageAlt: Equipment section with connected devices and network topology
gpon360.equipamentosImageCaption: Equipment section with device table and topology diagram
gpon360.dashboardTip: Tip: next to the TX Level, RX Level and Last Event fields there is a History button. It opens a window with graphs showing the evolution of these values over time, with periods of 3, 7, 15, or 30 days — or a custom period.
gpon360.dashboardEventHistory: In the specific case of the "Last Event" history, the window is even more complete: it shows the Connection Drop History, bringing how many drops occurred, the total time the client was offline, the duration of the longest drop, and the availability percentage (QoS), all with a graph and a color legend indicating the severity of each drop.
gpon360.signalMonitoringOverview: The Signal Monitoring screen is the control panel to track, in near real-time, the GPON signal quality of all clients in the database. With it you can quickly see where signal problems are — whether looking at the entire Brazil, a specific state, a city, a street, or even an individual client.
gpon360.signalOverviewImageAlt: Signal Monitoring screen with KPIs, city table, and rankings
gpon360.signalOverviewImageCaption: Overview of the Signal Monitoring screen.
gpon360.kpiIntro: Four cards summarize the scenario for the selected period:
gpon360.kpiTotalClientsDesc: Total number of GPON clients considered in the current filter.
gpon360.kpiOkRangeDesc: Clients with signal within the healthy range, displayed in green.
gpon360.kpiWarningRangeDesc: Clients in an alert zone, shown in orange/yellow.
gpon360.kpiCriticalRangeDesc: Clients with poor signal, shown in red.
gpon360.kpiCitiesCountDesc: How many locations are within the current filter scope.
gpon360.kpiAutoUpdate: These cards change automatically whenever you apply a filter, so they always reflect what is currently being displayed.
gpon360.periodFilterDesc: In the upper right corner you choose the analysis time window: 3d, 7d, 15d, or 30d. Next to it, the start and end dates of the selected range appear (e.g., "Jul 22 → Jul 28"). Simply click on the desired period button and all numbers, tables, and graphs on the screen are recalculated — just wait a few seconds for loading.
gpon360.citiesGponIntro: This is the heart of the screen, on the left side. Here you have two filters and a table:
gpon360.citiesItem1Desc: Dropdown menu with search. Click, type part of the state name (or scroll the list) and select. This restricts the entire screen to that state.
gpon360.citiesItem2Desc: Free text search: type part of the city name and the table filters instantly. This search only filters the city list — the summary cards continue showing totals from the state/period filter.
gpon360.citiesItem3Desc: Shows City, Clients, Critical, Warning, and a View button. Clicking on column headers (arrow icon) sorts ascending or descending — useful for finding the city with the most critical clients.
gpon360.citiesItem4Desc: This is the action to "enter" the city. The screen then shows the streets of that city, with a chip at the top indicating the active filter and an X to remove it.
gpon360.citiesItem5Desc: Below the table you define how many items per page you want to see (5, 10, 20, 50, 100, or 200) and navigate with previous/next page arrows.
gpon360.citiesDeepNavDesc1: After clicking "View" on a city, the table lists the streets with critical/warning signal. Clicking "View" on a street takes you to the most detailed level: the client list for that street, with contract, MAC, address, terminal (equipment model), signal in dBm, signal drops, status (OK, Warning, or Critical), and a Connect button that opens in a new tab the detailed panel for that client (modem information, QoS, Wi-Fi networks, etc.).
gpon360.citiesDeepNavDesc2: At this level there is also a search field by contract, MAC, or address, and a Download button to export the list — an action that asks for confirmation before executing, as it generates a file.
gpon360.citiesDeepNavTip: Tip: to go back to previous levels, simply click the X on the chips that appear next to the "Signal Monitoring" title.
gpon360.citiesImageAlt: GPON Cities table with state and city filters, ranking, and RX/TX level graphs
gpon360.citiesImageCaption: GPON Cities screen displaying filters, table, and rankings.
gpon360.rankingIntro: On the right side, this panel shows comparative rankings divided into three tabs:
gpon360.rankingCriticosDesc: Sorts locations by the percentage of clients with critical signal (below -27 dBm).
gpon360.rankingAtencaoDesc: Sorts by the percentage of clients in the warning range (-25 to -27 dBm).
gpon360.rankingMediaDesc: Sorts by the average signal level of the location — the more negative, the worse. Appears green when good and orange/red when bad.
gpon360.rankingClickNote: In each tab you can click on the Percentage/Value and Total columns to reorder results. Clicking on a city name in this ranking also lets you "enter" it, just like the View button in the table on the left.
gpon360.rankingImageAlt: Massive Trap ranking panel with Drop Events Rank and QoS Availability Rank
gpon360.rankingImageCaption: Detailed view of clients after navigating by city and street.
gpon360.rxTxGraphsIntro: When you filter by a specific state, city, or street, two line graphs appear at the bottom of the screen:
gpon360.rxGraphDesc: Shows the evolution of the signal level received by the client over the days of the selected period.
gpon360.txGraphDesc: Shows the evolution of the signal level transmitted by the equipment.
gpon360.rxTxGraphsOutro: These graphs help visualize whether the signal is improving, worsening, or stable over time.
gpon360.fluxoStep1: Choose the analysis period (3, 7, 15, or 30 days).
gpon360.fluxoStep2: Read the four indicators to understand the trap volume and average quality for the period.
gpon360.fluxoStep3: Use the State and City filters and table sorting to find critical locations.
gpon360.fluxoStep4: Check the ranking tabs to quickly identify the worst and best in line.
gpon360.fluxoStep5: Click "View" on the desired city to go down to the street level.
gpon360.fluxoStep6: Analyze the recalculated cards and ranking for that city and prioritize maintenance.
gpon360.trapOverview1: The Massive Trap screen (subtitle "GPON Trap Intelligence") is the intelligence panel that consolidates the traps — automatic technical alerts — sent by GPON network equipment.
gpon360.trapOverview2: Unlike the Fall Monitoring screen, which focuses on already classified drop events, this screen looks at the raw volume of trap records and two quality indicators — QoS availability and drop event rate — allowing you to see, hierarchically (country → state → city → street), where the network is performing better or worse.
gpon360.trapOverview3: You can find it in the left sidebar menu, under the Massive Trap option (antenna/sensor icon).
gpon360.trapPeriodDesc: In the upper right corner, the 3d, 7d, 15d, and 30d shortcuts define the analysis time window (default is the last 3 days). As with the falls screen, changing the period recalculates everything automatically.
gpon360.trapPeriodImageAlt: Massive Trap analysis period with 3, 7, 15, and 30-day shortcuts and KPIs
gpon360.kpiTotalRecordsDesc: Total number of traps received in the selected period.
gpon360.kpiCitiesDesc: Number of cities with records in the period. This card transforms into "Streets" when you enter the details of a specific city, maintaining the same hierarchical logic.
gpon360.kpiQosAvailabilityDesc: Average quality of service indicator, on a scale where 10 represents maximum availability. Appears green when at a good level.
gpon360.kpiDropEventsDesc: Average number of connection drop events, displayed in red — the lower, the better.
gpon360.citiesTableDesc: On the left side, a table lists each city — or each street, when you have already entered a city ("GPON Streets") — with four comparable columns:
gpon360.citiesResource1Desc: Dropdown list with internal search, available in the national view.
gpon360.citiesResource2Desc: Free text search. When entering the detail of a city, the filter becomes by Street.
gpon360.citiesResource3Desc: Click the arrows next to the column name — for example, sort by Total to find cities with the most records, or by QoS Avail. to find the worst ones.
gpon360.citiesResource4Desc: Choose 5, 10, 20, 50, 100, or 200 lines per page and navigate between pages.
gpon360.drillDownDesc: When clicking View on a city, the screen "dives" to the street level: a chip appears with the selected city name (with an "x" to remove it and return to the overview), the cards are recalculated only for that city, and the left table starts listing the streets within it. At this street level there is no additional detail button — the drill-down ends there.
gpon360.drillDownImageAlt: Massive Trap drill-down showing streets of São Paulo and drop event ranking
gpon360.rankingDesc: Two tabs allow comparing locations — cities or streets, depending on the level you are at — by two different criteria:
gpon360.ranking1Desc: Sorts from worst to best by the average drop events — the larger the red bar, the worse the situation.
gpon360.ranking2Desc: Sorts by QoS availability, highlighting with green bars the locations with the best performance.
gpon360.rankingOutro: Each ranking line shows the position, location name, a visual bar proportional to the indicator, and the associated record total — a quick way to identify both the "worst in line" and the "best in line" without having to manually reorder the table.
gpon360.fluxoStep7: Remove the city chip ("x") to return to the national view.
gpon360.trapOutro: In practice, this screen is aimed at network engineering and operations teams who need to prioritize maintenance actions based on aggregated technical data: identify which cities or streets concentrate the most traps and drop events, compare QoS performance between regions, and narrow the investigation from the national level down to the specific street generating the most network noise.
gpon360.fallOverview1: The Fall Monitoring screen is the control panel where you track, in near real-time, all connection drops happening on Claro's GPON network. It shows the current scenario visually (numbers and graphs) and also allows you to investigate each drop in detail, down to the affected client.
gpon360.fallOverview2: It is the ideal tool to quickly answer questions like "where are the problems now?", "which neighborhood/street is most affected?", and "which specific clients were impacted?".
gpon360.fallOverview3: You can find it in the left sidebar menu, under the Fall Monitoring option (power plug/disconnected icon).
gpon360.searchFiltersIntro: At the top of the screen you will find four filters that can be freely combined, in addition to the period selector:
gpon360.filter1Desc: Multiple state selection, with internal search field and "Select all" option.
gpon360.filter2Desc: Free text search: type the name of the desired city.
gpon360.filter3Desc: Filters by cause category: All, Power, Signal, or Other.
gpon360.filter4Desc: Selection of the specific optical center, also with text search among hundreds of equipment.
gpon360.filter5Desc: On the right side, quick shortcuts for the last 3, 7, 15, or 30 days.
gpon360.filterWarning: Warning: whenever you change a filter or the period, all numbers and graphs on the screen are recalculated automatically. This may take a few seconds, as it involves a large database.
gpon360.filterImageCaption: Available filters at the top of the Fall Monitoring screen.
gpon360.kpiIntro2: Right below the filters, six cards summarize the situation for the selected period/filter:
gpon360.kpiAffectedClientsDesc: Clients impacted by drops considered massive. When hovering over the info icon, the system explains that only occurrences affecting 3 or more clients in the same combination of state, city, OLT, and street are counted.
gpon360.kpiTotalFallsDesc: Number of massive drop events recorded, following the same criterion above.
gpon360.kpiSignalFallsDesc: How many of these drops were caused by optical signal issues.
gpon360.kpiPowerFallsDesc: How many were caused by power failure at the client's equipment.
gpon360.kpiAffectedCitiesDesc: Geographic scope of the problem in number of cities.
gpon360.kpiAffectedStreetsDesc: Geographic scope of the problem in number of streets.
gpon360.kpiPeakDesc: right below the cards, a red highlight shows the largest isolated occurrence — with location, date/time and number of affected clients — helping to quickly identify the most critical incident.
gpon360.kpiImageAlt: Fall Monitoring indicator cards with affected clients, total drops, signal drops, power drops, affected cities and streets
gpon360.kpiImageCaption: Main indicators and period peak highlight.
gpon360.chart1Desc: Bar chart comparing the volume of drops across all states. Important: this chart always shows the overall total, ignoring applied filters — it works as a "snapshot" of the national context.
gpon360.chart2Desc: Line chart with the number of drops aggregated by hour, allowing you to see peaks and patterns throughout the selected period.
gpon360.chartImageAlt: Drops by State and Timeline charts from Fall Monitoring
gpon360.chartImageCaption: Comparison by state and temporal evolution of drops.
gpon360.fallsTableIntro: This is the detailed, event-by-event list with the following columns:
gpon360.fallsTableCol9: Drop type (cause code and technical description)
gpon360.fallsRes1Desc: Search by Street or by NAP (optical distribution box identifier).
gpon360.fallsRes2Desc: Click the arrows next to "Affected Clients" and "When" to reorder.
gpon360.fallsRes3Desc: Choose 5, 10, 20, 50, 100, or 200 lines per page and navigate between pages.
gpon360.fallsRes4Desc: Exports the filtered table data to a file, useful for external reports.
gpon360.fallsTableImageAlt: GPON Connection Drops table with Street and NAP filters
gpon360.fallsTableImageCaption: Detailed view of the GPON connection drops table.
gpon360.fallDetailDesc1: When clicking View on any table row, the screen transforms into a focused view on that specific event (street, city, and time), showing a summary — affected clients, total drops, signal and power drops — and a list with each individually impacted client: contract, equipment MAC address, address, terminal model (ONU/router), and how many drops that specific client had.
gpon360.fallDetailDesc2: In this list there is also a Connect button, which opens in a new tab the Dashboard for that client, allowing you to start a remote diagnosis directly on their equipment — a bridge between macro monitoring and individual service.
gpon360.fallDetailImageAlt: Detail screen of the View action with summary and affected clients
gpon360.fallDetailImageCaption: Detailed view after clicking View on a drop event.
gpon360.fallFluxoStep1: Choose the analysis period (3, 7, 15, or 30 days).
gpon360.fallFluxoStep2: Combine the State, City, Drop Type, and OLT filters as needed for the investigation.
gpon360.fallFluxoStep3: Read the six indicators and the "Period Peak" highlight to prioritize the most critical incident.
gpon360.fallFluxoStep4: Use the charts to understand distribution by state and hourly peaks.
gpon360.fallFluxoStep5: Locate the event in the table using the Street or NAP search and sorting.
gpon360.fallFluxoStep6: Click "View" to open the event detail and the list of impacted clients.
gpon360.fallFluxoStep7: Use "Connect" to open the client's Dashboard and start remote diagnosis.
gpon360.fallOutro: In practice, this screen helps operations and support teams quickly identify regions with network problems, understand whether the predominant cause is power or optical signal, prioritize service based on the "period peak", and navigate from the general problem down to the specific affected client without switching systems.
gpon360.perfWhatIs: The Contractual Performance screen exists to answer a very practical question: "Are clients actually receiving the internet speed they contracted?". Instead of looking at drops or network traps, the focus here is on delivery quality — comparing the speed measured on equipment with what was contracted, allowing you to see this performance by region, equipment model, and installed firmware version.
gpon360.perfWhatIs2: You can find it in the left sidebar menu, under the Performance option (ascending chart icon).
gpon360.perfSearchIntro: Unlike other monitoring screens, here the screen does not load data automatically. It starts empty, showing only the Filters block, and only fetches information when you fill in at least one criterion and click Search. The available filters are:
gpon360.perfFilter4Desc: Equipment model installed at the client's home (e.g., HG8245H).
gpon360.perfFilter5Desc: Firmware/software version running on the equipment.
gpon360.perfFilterWarning: Warning: filters can be freely combined and the Clear button resets everything at once. Very broad searches (an entire state without restricting city or period) can take a long time or even return an unavailability error, as they involve processing a large volume of data — the ideal is to always refine by city, OLT, or a shorter period.
gpon360.perfFilterImageAlt: Contractual Performance filter and KPI interface showing State, City, Node/OLT, Model, SW Version, Period, and average delivered speed cards
gpon360.perfFilterImageCaption: Filter block and initial cards of Contractual Performance.
gpon360.perfKpiAvgSpeedDesc: Average adherence percentage between measured and contracted speed (e.g., 123% means that, on average, analyzed clients are receiving even more than contracted). Clicking "More information" opens a detailed panel with total contracts, average, minimum, maximum, standard deviation, and percentiles 25, 50 (median), and 75 — great for deeper statistical analysis.
gpon360.perfKpiBelowThresholdsDesc: Three indicators showing the share of clients whose measured speed fell below these thresholds (i.e., delivering less than they should). Each also has its "More information", revealing the total evaluated, how many fell below the threshold, and the corresponding percentage.
gpon360.perfKpiDirectlyEvaluatedDesc: Shows how many contracts, out of the total filtered, had their speed effectively measured in the period (e.g., 900 out of 26,233 contracts, or 3%). This number contextualizes the reliability of the other indicators, showing the actual sample size behind the percentages.
gpon360.perfKpiImageAlt: Contractual Performance main indicator cards: average delivered speed and percentages of clients below thresholds
gpon360.perfChart1Desc: Histogram showing how many terminals fall into each adherence range (≥100%, 90–99%, 80–89%, 70–79%, <70%), allowing you to quickly see whether the majority of clients are well served or not.
gpon360.perfChart2Desc: Horizontal bar chart comparing the average delivered speed by terminal/ONU model, useful for identifying if any specific model is performing below expectations.
gpon360.perfChart3Desc: Same logic, but comparing by firmware version — helps identify if a specific software version is causing performance loss.
gpon360.perfChart4Desc: Comparison of average performance between states (or, when filtered, between the returned locations).
gpon360.perfChartImageAlt: Contractual Performance visual analysis charts: performance distribution, by model, software version, and by state
gpon360.perfEquipTableIntro: A detailed table crossing Model and SW Version, with columns:
gpon360.perfEquipTableSortNote: All columns are sortable (clicking the arrows), the number of items per page is adjustable, pagination is available to navigate results, and there is an Export CSV button to download this data. This table is excellent for quickly identifying specific equipment + firmware combinations that are performing poorly.
gpon360.perfEquipImageAlt: Equipment & Firmware table from Contractual Performance with columns Model, SW Version, Total Clients, Download (%), % below 80%, and % below 70%
gpon360.perfRegionalTableIntro: Similar to the previous one, but organized by State (UF) and City:
gpon360.perfRegionalSortNote: It is also sortable and has its own Export CSV button, allowing you to compare performance between different serviced regions.
gpon360.perfRegionalImageAlt: Regional Performance table from Contractual Performance with columns State, City, Total Clients, Download (%), % below 80%, and % below 70%
gpon360.perfFlowTitle: What is it for, in practice?
gpon360.perfFluxoStep1: Fill in at least one filter (ideally city, OLT, or short period) and click Search.
gpon360.perfFluxoStep2: Read the indicator cards to understand the average adherence and the share of clients below thresholds.
gpon360.perfFluxoStep3: Check "Directly Evaluated Clients" to gauge the actual sample size behind the percentages.
gpon360.perfFluxoStep4: Use the charts to identify patterns by range, model, software version, and state.
gpon360.perfFluxoStep5: Dive into the Equipment & Firmware table to find critical equipment + firmware combinations.
gpon360.perfFluxoStep6: Compare locations in the Regional Performance table and export data to CSV when needed.
gpon360.perfOutro: This screen is aimed at engineering, quality, and product teams who need to ensure the contractual speed promise is being fulfilled. With it, you can check whether a specific equipment model or firmware version is delivering less than it should, compare performance across different cities or states, and quickly identify which slice of the client base is receiving speed below what was agreed — supporting decisions on equipment replacement, firmware updates, or targeted commercial/technical actions.
gpon360.reportsWhatIs1: The Analytical Reports screen is the dedicated space to download complete and detailed reports automatically generated by the GPON system, one per day. Unlike the monitoring screens (which show visual and interactive dashboards), the goal here is simple and direct: give you access to raw data files, ready for download, that can be used in external analysis, audits, or integrations with other tools.
gpon360.reportsWhatIs2: You can find it in the left sidebar menu, under the Reports option (document/receipt icon).
gpon360.reportsImageAlt: Analytical Reports screen with period filter, daily reports table, and download columns
gpon360.reportsImageCaption: Main Analytical Reports screen, with date filter and list of reports available for download.
gpon360.reportsFilterDesc: At the top of the screen, the Filter new analytical report block allows you to choose a date range (fields "Period" and "Until") to narrow the list of displayed reports. After setting the dates, just click Search to update the list. If you want to return to the default view, the Clear button clears the date fields — note that with empty fields, the screen shows the message "No report found for the selected period", so the ideal is to always set new dates or reload the page to see the full list again.
gpon360.reportsTableIntro: Below the filter, a table lists the generated reports, with columns:
gpon360.reportsColTypeDesc: For now, all appear as "Analytical report".
gpon360.reportsColDateDesc: Reference day of the report (reports are generated daily).
gpon360.reportsColSizeDesc: File size, around 180 to 230 MB — an indication that these are robust reports with a large volume of data.
gpon360.reportsColActionsDesc: Download link for each row, allowing you to download that specific day's report.
gpon360.reportsDefaultNote: By default, the screen displays reports from the last 15 days, with simple pagination at the bottom (first page, previous, current page number, and next/last page buttons).
gpon360.reportsUsageTitle: What is it for, in practice?
gpon360.reportsUsageIntro: This screen is the official channel for those who need the raw GPON operation data outside the system itself. It is useful for:
gpon360.reportsUsage1: Feeding external spreadsheets and dashboards with raw GPON operation data.
gpon360.reportsUsage2: Cross-referencing network information with other company databases.
gpon360.reportsUsage3: Generating customized management reports outside the platform.
gpon360.reportsUsage4: Archiving the daily network history for audits and compliance.
gpon360.reportsWarning: Warning: as the files are large (in the range of hundreds of MB), the download may take a few moments depending on your connection. We recommend downloading only the days you really need using the period filter, instead of downloading everything at once.
gpon360.paramWhatIs: The Parameter Management screen, available in the GPON system sidebar (settings/tune icon), is the panel where the team configures the rules that define whether a network technical indicator is in Good, Fair, or Poor status. In other words, this is where you define, for each monitored metric, which value ranges represent good functioning and which represent a problem.
gpon360.paramPurposeDesc: Think of it as the "rules brain" behind the monitoring panels (Dashboard, Signal Monitoring, Performance, etc.). Instead of the system deciding on its own what is a good or bad signal, it is on this screen that the team manually configures these limits, ensuring that the alerts and classifications shown in other areas of the system reflect the criteria defined by the operations team.
gpon360.paramPurposeImageAlt: Available Parameters table with Parameter Name and Actions columns, showing View details and Edit buttons
gpon360.paramPurposeImageCaption: Available Parameters card with the paginated list of configurable indicators.
gpon360.paramScreenDesc1: Just below the Parameter Management title, there is a card called Available Parameters, which lists all configurable indicators in table format, with two columns: the parameter name and the available actions for it. The list is paginated — on the first page 10 parameters appear, and on the second, 3 more, totaling 13 items. Navigation between pages is done through the arrows at the bottom of the card.
gpon360.paramScreenDesc2: The parameters cover quite varied areas of operation:
gpon360.paramCat2Params: TX of optical signals, RX of optical signals
gpon360.paramCat3Params: Availability, Availability QoS Calculation, QoS Availability
gpon360.paramViewIntro: When clicking View details next to any parameter, a window opens showing how that indicator is currently configured. The ranges appear organized into three colored groups:
gpon360.paramGoodDesc: range considered healthy/ideal for the indicator.
gpon360.paramRegularDesc: alert range, outside the ideal but not yet critical.
gpon360.paramBadDesc: critical range, indicates a problem that warrants action.
gpon360.paramViewDesc: Each one displays the minimum ("From") and maximum ("To") values for that range. The same group can have more than one value range — for example, the TX optical signal parameter has two different ranges classified as "Good", covering both positive and negative values, since optical signals are measured in dBm. This window is for quick reference only, functioning as a summary before eventual editing.
gpon360.paramViewStep1: Click View details next to the desired parameter.
gpon360.paramViewStep2: Check the ranges organized by Good, Fair, and Poor.
gpon360.paramViewStep3: Each range displays the minimum (From) and maximum (To) values.
gpon360.paramViewStep4: Use as a summary before editing or to validate current rules.
gpon360.paramEditDesc1: The Edit button opens an editable version of the same window, allowing you to adjust the "From" and "To" values of each range directly in the numeric fields. Each category (Good, Fair, Poor) has a + button next to its name, which allows adding a new value range to that classification, and each additional range gets a trash icon to be removed if no longer needed. After adjusting the desired values, the Save button in the bottom right corner confirms the changes.
gpon360.paramEditDesc2: It is worth noting that not all parameters already have registered ranges: when consulting the Latency parameter, for example, the window appears empty, indicating that this configuration still needs to be defined by the responsible team.
gpon360.paramEditStep1: Click Edit to open the editable version of the window.
gpon360.paramEditStep2: Adjust the From and To values in the numeric fields.
gpon360.paramEditStep3: Use the + button next to each category to add new ranges.
gpon360.paramEditStep4: Remove unnecessary ranges with the trash icon.
gpon360.paramEditStep5: Click Save to confirm the changes.
gpon360.paramEditImageAlt: QoS Wifi parameter editing modal with From and To fields for Good, Poor, and Fair classifications
gpon360.paramEditImageCaption: QoS Wifi parameter editing modal, allowing adjustment of value ranges by classification.
gpon360.paramWhyDesc: The "Good", "Fair", and "Poor" ranges defined here feed other system screens (such as signal monitoring, performance, and reports), serving as a reference to automatically identify when a client or equipment is outside expected standards. Therefore, keeping these parameters well calibrated is important so that alerts and indicators throughout the rest of the platform are reliable.
gpon360.auditWhatIs: The Audit Log screen, accessible from the GPON system sidebar (document/portrait icon), works as the historical record of all actions performed by users within the platform. It is a kind of "system logbook": every query, search, or operation made by anyone on the team is recorded here, with date, time, author, and details of the executed action.
gpon360.auditPurposeDesc: This screen exists to provide transparency and traceability to system operations. It allows the team (usually supervisors, security, or support) to answer questions like:
gpon360.auditPurposeQ3: "What operations did a specific user perform today?"
gpon360.auditPurposeOutro: It is an essential audit and compliance tool, very common in systems that handle sensitive client data.
gpon360.auditFilterDesc: At the top of the page is the filters card, where you can refine the search by user name, email, operation type, and a date range (Period and Until fields). There is also the "Filter most recent log by user" option, which, when checked, likely brings only the most recent record of each user instead of the full history. Next to the filters are the Search button, which executes the query, and Clear, which resets all filled fields.
gpon360.auditFilterImportant: Important: filling in both dates (start and end of the period) is mandatory to perform any search. If any field is left empty, the system displays the warning "Both dates must be filled in." and the query is not executed.
gpon360.auditTableDesc: The second block displays the results table with the main columns. The Operation column is especially detailed: besides the action name (like
gpon360.auditTableDescEnd: ), it also shows the technical parameters used in that query, such as city code, contract number, MAC address, or searched dates.
gpon360.auditColUserDesc: Name of the person who performed the action within the platform.
gpon360.auditColEmailDesc: Email address linked to the user who executed the operation.
gpon360.auditColOperationDesc: Name of the executed action (e.g., client search or connection) along with the technical parameters used, such as city code, contract number, MAC address, or searched dates.
gpon360.auditColDateDesc: Exact date and time when the action was recorded.
gpon360.auditFilterImageAlt: Audit Log filter card with user name, email, operation, and date range fields
gpon360.auditResources1: Just above the table is the Export CSV button, which allows you to download the filtered records to a spreadsheet. The table also has pagination at the bottom, with arrows to advance or go back pages and an "Items per page" selector, with options of 5, 10, 20, or 50 records at a time — useful depending on how much data you need to view at once.
gpon360.auditResources2: By default, the screen loads records from the last 24 hours, but the total data volume is large (the system already accumulates thousands of records), so filters are essential to quickly find what you are looking for.
gpon360.auditResourceImageAlt: Audit Log results table with Export CSV button, User, Email, Operation, and Date columns, and pagination
gpon360.auditResourceImageCaption: Audit Log results table with export and pagination
gpon360.auditHowToTitle: How to use — step by step
gpon360.auditStep1: Make sure the Period and Until fields are filled in (both are mandatory).
gpon360.auditStep2: Enter the user name in the User Name field to investigate a specific person's actions.
gpon360.auditStep3: Use the Operation field to filter by a type of action, such as Connect Client.
gpon360.auditStep4: Combine filters (email, operation type, and dates) for more precise results.
gpon360.auditStep5: Click Search to execute the query. Use Clear to reset the filters.
gpon360.auditInferredTitle: What can be inferred about this screen
gpon360.auditInferredDesc: Given the richness of recorded technical details (MAC addresses, contract numbers, city codes, equipment serials), this screen seems to automatically capture every relevant call made in other areas of the GPON system, such as Clients, Signal Monitoring, and Performance. In other words, the Audit Log is not a screen where you manually register anything — it is automatically fed by the system itself, serving purely as a query and export panel for history.
gpon360.auditTipDesc: If you already know the name or email of the person you want to investigate, it is worth using the "Filter most recent log by user" option to go directly to the last recorded action, saving time instead of browsing through several pages of results. And always remember to adjust the date period before searching, as it is mandatory and defaults to the last 24 hours.
